s: For what period was Hyderabad to function as the common capital under Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Section 5 provided for Hyderabad to serve as the common capital for up to ten years, after which it would be the capital of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh would have a new capital.

s: What do Sections 7 and 8 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provide for?
o: They provide for the national project status of Polavaram.
They provide for the Apex Council and the two river management boards.
They provide for a common Governor and the Governor's special responsibility in the common capital.
They provide for tax incentives and capital infrastructure support.
x: Sections 7 and 8 deal with the common Governor and the Governor's special responsibility in the common capital.

s: Which training centre in Hyderabad was made a common training centre for both successor States for a maximum of three years under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy
x: The Act let the Greyhound Training Centre, Hyderabad, serve both States as a common training centre for up to three years.

s: Under Section 8 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, who appoints the two advisors who assist the common Governor?
o: The Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh
x: For his special responsibility in the common capital, the Governor is helped by two advisors appointed by the Centre.

s: How many districts formed the State of Telangana under Section 3 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Section 3 formed Telangana from 10 districts; residual Andhra Pradesh had 13 districts.

s: Under Section 3 of the AP Reorganisation Act, as amended by the Polavaram Ordinance, villages of which district in the Polavaram submergence area stayed with Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Polavaram Ordinance amended Section 3 so that Khammam villages in the Polavaram submergence area stayed with AP.

s: For what period was Hyderabad designated as the common capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
x: Section 5 made Hyderabad, meaning the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation area, the common capital for not more than ten years.

s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides for a common Governor for both States?
x: Section 7 provides for a common Governor; Section 3 forms Telangana, Section 5 makes Hyderabad the common capital and Section 6 sets up the expert committee.

s: How does the Governor act in discharging his special responsibility in the common capital?
o: On the advice of the Telangana Council of Ministers
In his individual judgment after consulting the Telangana Council of Ministers
On the advice of the Andhra Pradesh Council of Ministers
On the advice of both State Legislatures
x: The Governor exercises individual judgment after consulting the Telangana Council of Ministers, and the decision is final.

s: Under Section 8, whom does the Governor consult in discharging his special responsibility?
x: He uses individual judgment after consulting the Telangana Council of Ministers, and his decision is final.

s: Under Section 7 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, who decides the period for which one Governor serves both States?
x: Section 7 provides one Governor for both States for such period as the President may determine.

s: On which date did the territorial bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh take effect (the appointed day)?
x: The Act was enacted on 1 March 2014 (President's assent), but the territorial split took effect on the appointed day, 2 June 2014.

s: On which date was the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill introduced in the Lok Sabha?
x: It was introduced on 13 February 2014, passed by the Lok Sabha on 18 February and by the Rajya Sabha on 20 February.

s: On which date did the Rajya Sabha pass the AP Reorganisation Bill by voice vote, without amendment?
x: The Rajya Sabha passed it on 20 February 2014; the Lok Sabha had passed it on 18 February.

s: Who was the President of India when the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 received assent?
x: President Pranab Mukherjee gave assent on 1 March 2014.

s: Section 10 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 amended the First Schedule of the Constitution to make Telangana which State of India?
x: Section 10 amended the First Schedule of the Constitution and recognised Telangana as the 29th State of India.

s: Which Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with the allotment of sitting members of the Rajya Sabha?
x: The First Schedule provides for allotment of sitting Rajya Sabha members and is linked with Section 13.

s: For how long was the State Load Despatch Centre to be shared under Schedule XII of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: The SLDC was shared for up to two years, while APERC acted as a joint regulator for up to six months.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Eleventh Schedule — Coal, oil and gas and power
Eighth Schedule — Government companies and corporations
Ninth Schedule — Apportionment of pension liability
Tenth Schedule — Continuance of facilities in State institutions
x: The Tenth Schedule concerns continuance of facilities in State institutions, such as APSCHE and Shilparamam. The Eighth concerns pension liability, the Ninth concerns companies and corporations, and the Eleventh concerns river management boards.

s: Which Schedule lays down the principles for the Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards?
x: Schedule XI contains the principles for the Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards.

s: Under Schedule XI of the AP Reorganisation Act, which use is given precedence over irrigation?
x: Schedule XI gives drinking water precedence over irrigation, and irrigation precedence over power.

s: Which Schedule of the A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014 contains the 'List of Funds' such as provident, pension and insurance funds?
x: The Seventh Schedule is the List of Funds (asked in APPSC 2022). The Eighth deals with pension liability apportionment, the Tenth with continuance of facilities in State institutions, and the Twelfth with coal, oil and gas, and power.

s: Which of the following Schedules of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 is correctly matched with its subject?
o: Schedule XI – Coal, oil, gas and power
x: Schedule IX covers companies and corporations; VII is funds, VIII pension liability and XII coal, oil, gas and power.

s: The apportionment of pension liability is dealt with in which Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act?
x: The Eighth Schedule (Section 59) apportions pension liability.

s: For how long was APERC to act as the joint regulator under Schedule XII?
x: APERC was joint regulator for up to six months; the SLDC was shared for up to two years.

s: Which Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 lists 107 State institutions, such as APSCHE, whose facilities continue for both States?
x: The Tenth Schedule lists 107 State institutions (e.g. APSCHE, Shilparamam) whose facilities continue for both States.

s: Which Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 contains amendments to the Delimitation Order, 2008?
x: The Second Schedule (Section 15) amends the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 2008.

s: Which Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with coal, oil and gas, and power?
x: The Twelfth Schedule covers coal, oil and gas, and power; the Eleventh covers the river management boards.

s: The Fifth and Sixth Schedules of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 amend which of the following?
o: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 and the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950
The Delimitation Order, 2008 and the RP Act, 1950
The First and Fourth Schedules of the Constitution
The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the RP Act, 1951
x: Schedules V and VI of the Act amend the Constitution (SC) Order 1950 and the Constitution (ST) Order 1950.

s: How many Parts, sections and Schedules does the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 have?
x: The Act has 12 Parts, 108 sections and 13 Schedules.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 is which numbered Act of 2014?
x: It is Act No. 6 of 2014, published in Gazette No. 6.

s:
Consider the following statements about the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. It divided the old State into two States, Telangana and residual Andhra Pradesh.
2. Telangana became the 29th State of India.
3. The Act has 12 Schedules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Act created Telangana as the 29th State; it has 13 Schedules, not 12.

s: Which Part of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with authorisation of expenditure and distribution of revenues?
x: Part V covers expenditure and distribution of revenues; Part VI is assets and liabilities and Part VIII is services.

s: After reorganisation in 2014, how many Lok Sabha seats does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: Andhra Pradesh has 25 Lok Sabha seats and Telangana 17; in the Assemblies the figures are 175 and 119.

s: Under which Article could each Governor nominate one Anglo-Indian MLA, as allowed by Section 18 of the AP Reorganisation Act?
x: Section 18 provided for one nominated Anglo-Indian member in each Assembly under Article 333 (the provision was later ended by the 104th Amendment).

s: Which of the following seat allocations after reorganisation is correctly matched?
x: AP got 11 and Telangana 7 of the 18 Rajya Sabha seats; Lok Sabha is 25 and 17, Assembly 175 and 119.

s: In 2014, which district of Andhra Pradesh had the most Assembly constituencies?
x: East Godavari had the most (19), followed by Guntur (17).

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh had the fewest Assembly constituencies (9) in 2014?
x: Vizianagaram had 9 seats, the fewest; Srikakulam, Nellore and YSR Kadapa had 10 each.

s: Of the 175 Assembly seats of Andhra Pradesh, how many are reserved for SCs and STs respectively?
x: 29 seats are reserved for SCs and 7 for STs.

s: How many members may the Legislative Council of Andhra Pradesh have under the AP Reorganisation Act?
x: AP's Council can have not more than 50 members; Telangana's has 40.

s: Under Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, to how many seats can the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly be raised from 175?
x: Section 26 allows delimitation to raise the AP Assembly from 175 to 225 seats, subject to Article 170.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment ended the nomination of one Anglo-Indian MLA provided under Section 18 of the AP Reorganisation Act?
x: Section 18 used Article 333 for Anglo-Indian nomination; the 104th Amendment ended this provision.

s: How many seats does the Telangana Legislative Assembly have under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: The Act gave Andhra Pradesh 175 and Telangana 119 Assembly seats, out of the earlier 294.

s: How many members does the Telangana Legislative Council have under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Telangana's Legislative Council has 40 members; the AP Council has not more than 50.

s: Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 allows the AP Assembly to be raised from 175 to 225 seats subject to which Article of the Constitution?
x: Section 26 permits delimitation to raise the seats from 175 to 225, subject to Article 170 on the composition of Legislative Assemblies.

s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, which Schedules of the Constitution were amended?
x: Section 10 amended the First Schedule, while the Fourth Schedule was amended to revise the Rajya Sabha representation of Andhra Pradesh and provide an entry for Telangana.

s: The First Schedule of which enactment was amended in relation to Lok Sabha seats following the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The First Schedule of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 was amended for the allocation of Lok Sabha seats. The Representation of the People Act, 1951 was amended separately through Section 15A for the Telangana Legislative Council.

s: Under Section 30 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, till when was the High Court at Hyderabad to remain common to both States?
o: The Governor of Telangana issued a notification
The expiry of ten years from the appointed day, irrespective of any new High Court
A separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh was set up under Article 214
The new State capitals were finalised by Parliament
x: The Hyderabad High Court remained common to both States until a separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh was established under Article 214.

s: The separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh was constituted by a Presidential order under which Article?
x: The 26 December 2018 order was made under Article 214 and the Act.

s: Which Section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides for a separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh?
x: Section 31 provides a separate High Court for AP; Section 30 kept the Hyderabad High Court common in the meantime.

s: From which date did the High Court of Andhra Pradesh begin functioning with its principal seat at Amaravati?
x: After the Presidential order of 26 December 2018, the AP High Court began functioning at Amaravati on 1 January 2019.

s: On which date was the Presidential order issued constituting a separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Presidential order of 26 December 2018 under Article 214 and the Act constituted the separate AP High Court, which began work on 1 January 2019.

s:
Consider the following statements about the High Court of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 named Amaravati as the seat of the AP High Court.
2. After the AP High Court began functioning, the Hyderabad court became the High Court for Telangana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Act named no place for the AP High Court; on 1 January 2019 the AP High Court began at Amaravati and the Hyderabad court became Telangana's High Court.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Krishna River Management Board under Section 85 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Section 85 places the KRMB in Andhra Pradesh and the Godavari River Management Board in Telangana.

s: Who chairs the Apex Council constituted under Section 84 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Chief Ministers of both States jointly
x: The Apex Council is chaired by the Union Water Resources Minister, with the Chief Ministers of both States as members.

s: Under which Section of the A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014 was the Polavaram Irrigation Project declared a national project?
x: Section 90 declared Polavaram a national project, with Telangana's consent deemed given. Section 84 is the Apex Council, Section 89 extends the KWDT term (a common wrong answer), and Section 93 deals with Thirteenth Schedule measures.

s: Which provision of Section 94 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 is correctly matched?
o: Section 94(2) – Special support for the new capital
Section 94(3) – Denotification of degraded forest land
Section 94(1) – Fiscal measures including tax incentives
x: 94(1) covers fiscal measures, 94(2) backward-area infrastructure, 94(3) special support for the new capital and 94(4) denotification of degraded forest land.

s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 extended the term of the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal?
x: Section 89 extends the KWDT term for project-wise allocation; Section 90 is Polavaram.

s: Which of the following pairs under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 is NOT correctly matched?
o: Apex Council – chaired by the Union Water Resources Minister
x: The GRMB has its headquarters in Telangana; the KRMB is in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Within what period was the Centre to take the Thirteenth Schedule measures under Section 93?
x: Section 93 gives the Centre 10 years to take the Thirteenth Schedule measures.

s: Under which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act was the 13th Finance Commission award split by population ratio and other parameters?
x: Section 46 splits the 13th FC award and provides a special development package for backward areas.

s: Which of the following parts of Section 94 is correctly matched?
o: 94(4) – Denotifying degraded forest land for the capital
x: 94(4) is denotifying degraded forest land for the capital; 94(1) is tax incentives, 94(2) backward-area infrastructure and 94(3) the new capital.

s: What does Section 95 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deal with?
o: Equal opportunities for quality higher education
x: Section 95 ensures equal opportunities for quality higher education to all students of both States.

s: Which constitutional provision was amended to include Telangana among the States having a Legislative Council?
x: Section 96 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act amended Article 168(1)(a) to add Telangana to the States with a Legislative Council.

s: After the amendment made by the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, to which State or States does Article 371D refer?
x: Section 97 amended Article 371D so that it reads “Andhra Pradesh or Telangana.”

s: Which Section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 was amended by the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 for the Telangana Legislative Council?
x: Section 98 of the AP Reorganisation Act amended Section 15A of the RP Act, 1951 for the Telangana Council.

s: Under Section 105 of the AP Reorganisation Act, who finally decided disputes over the transfer of pending cases?
x: Section 105 sent disputes on transferring pending cases to the Hyderabad High Court, whose decision was final.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly resolution of 28 March 2026 requested that which words be inserted in Section 5(2)?
x: The Assembly resolution requested the insertion of the words “at Amaravati” in Section 5(2), following the High Court's order of 3 March 2022.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 was the first law in which Parliament did what?
o: Amended the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution
Created a Legislative Council for a State
x: The 2026 amendment was described as the first instance of Parliament naming a State's capital by law.

s: On which date did the AP Assembly pass the resolution to insert 'at Amaravati' in Section 5(2)?
x: The resolution was passed on 28 March 2026; Parliament passed the amendment in April 2026.

s: On which date did the Andhra Pradesh High Court pass its order on the capital (Amaravati)?
x: The High Court order on the capital was given on 3 March 2022.

s: After bifurcation, residuary Andhra Pradesh received about what share of revenue while bearing a larger share of debt?
x: Residuary AP received about 46% of the revenue but had to bear a larger share of the debt.

s: What is the population ratio (Census 2011) used for apportionment between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
x: AP 58.32 : Telangana 41.68 is the Census 2011 population ratio. D reverses it; 46% is AP's share of revenue/power, not population; 50:50 is not used.

s: How much was released for the Section 46(2) resource gap of Andhra Pradesh in 2014-15?
x: ₹2,303 crore was released in 2014-15, ₹500 crore in 2015-16 and ₹1,176.50 crore in 2016-17, totalling ₹3,979.50 crore.

s: The grant for backward districts of Andhra Pradesh is ₹350 crore a year for how many districts?
x: ₹350 crore a year goes to 7 backward districts of Rayalaseema and North Coastal AP.

s: How much total special assistance had been released to Andhra Pradesh by March 2018, including Rs 2,500 crore for the capital?
x: By March 2018 the total special assistance released was Rs 12,476.76 crore, of which Rs 2,500 crore was for the capital.

s: How much was disbursed under Section 94(3) of the AP Reorganisation Act as special support for the new capital?
x: ₹2,500 crore was disbursed under Section 94(3) for the new capital (Raj Bhavan, High Court, Secretariat, Assembly, Council).

s: Which of the following pairs of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 is correctly matched?
o: Section 46 – Grants and special development package for backward areas
Section 47 – Polavaram declared a national project
Section 90 – Common Governor for both States
x: Section 46 provides grants and a special development package for backward areas, especially Rayalaseema and the north coastal districts. Common capital is Sec 5, Polavaram is Sec 90 and the common Governor is Sec 7.

s: Which provision of the AP Reorganisation Act provides fiscal measures including tax incentives?
x: 94(1) covers tax incentives; 94(2) backward-area infrastructure and 94(3) the new capital.

s: What does Section 46(2) of the AP Reorganisation Act provide for?
o: The Centre meeting the resource gap of residual AP
x: Under Section 46(2) the Centre meets the resource shortage of residual Andhra Pradesh.

s: Under the general principle for division of assets and liabilities between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, which basis was applied respectively to assets and liabilities?
o: Assets on population basis and liabilities on location basis
Assets on location basis and liabilities on population basis
Both assets and liabilities on area basis
Both assets and liabilities on revenue-contribution basis
x: Assets were generally divided on the basis of location, whereas liabilities or debt were divided on the basis of population.

s: Although Andhra Pradesh accounted for about 58 per cent of the population, it received what share of power under the last five years’ average-consumption basis?
x: Andhra Pradesh had about 58 per cent of the population but received only 46 per cent of the power under the stated sharing basis.

s:
Consider the following statements about the division of assets under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. Assets and commercial undertakings (Section 53) are divided by population ratio.
2. Treasury and bank cash balances (Section 49) are divided by population ratio.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Cash balances under Section 49 go by population ratio; assets and commercial undertakings under Section 53 go by location, so statement 1 is wrong.

s: On what basis are the Seventh Schedule funds (provident, pension and insurance funds) divided under Section 52?
x: Seventh Schedule funds are divided by population ratio under Section 52.

s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act deals with tax refunds, shared in the ratio 58.32 : 41.68?
x: Section 56 shares tax refunds by population ratio; AP's loss was about ₹3,900 crore.

s: Which of the following institutions is NOT included among the educational commitments in Schedule XIII?
x: Schedule XIII includes an IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER, Central, Petroleum and Agricultural Universities, an IIIT, an AIIMS-type hospital, a Tribal University and NIDM. An Indian Institute of Science is not listed.

s: Where is the Petroleum University, established as the Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy, located?
x: The Petroleum University, or IIPE, is located at Visakhapatnam. It was established by an Act of Parliament in 2017.

s: Where is the AIIMS set up in Andhra Pradesh under the AP Reorganisation Act located?
x: AIIMS is at Mangalagiri; NIT is at Tadepalligudem, IIT at Tirupati and IIM at Visakhapatnam.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Central Tribal University is located at Vizianagaram, not Nellore. IISER is at Tirupati, IIITDM at Kurnool and the Central University at Anantapur.

s: In which year was the Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy in Andhra Pradesh set up by an Act?
x: IIPE was set up by an Act of 2017; the Central Tribal University came through the Central Universities (Amendment) Act, 2019.

s:
Consider the following statements about central institutions in Andhra Pradesh:
1. IISER is located at Tirupati.
2. IIPE is located at Visakhapatnam.
3. IIITDM is located at Kurnool.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: IISER (with IIT) is at Tirupati, IIPE (with IIM) at Visakhapatnam and IIITDM at Kurnool.

s: Where is the Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The Central Tribal University is at Vizianagaram; the Central University is at Anantapur.

s: Where is the NIT of Andhra Pradesh located?
x: NIT is at Tadepalligudem; AIIMS is at Mangalagiri and IIIT at Sri City.

s: Where is the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) set up for Andhra Pradesh under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 located?
x: The IIT for Andhra Pradesh is at Tirupati, which also has the IISER.

s: In which city is the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) of Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The IIM of Andhra Pradesh is at Visakhapatnam, which also has the IIPE.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Institution)
A. IIITDM
B. AIIMS
C. Central University
D. IIIT
List-II (Location)
1. Sri City
2. Kurnool
3. Mangalagiri
4. Anantapur
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: IIITDM is at Kurnool, AIIMS at Mangalagiri, the Central University at Anantapur and the IIIT at Sri City.

s: How many premier central institutions set up under the AP Reorganisation Act are functional in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The notes record 11 premier institutions, such as IIT, IIM, NIT, IISER and AIIMS, as functional.

s: Under which Act were the Central University at Anantapur and the Central Tribal University at Vizianagaram set up?
x: Both universities in Andhra Pradesh were provided for by the Central Universities (Amendment) Act, 2019.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the infrastructure commitments in the Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: The Vizag-Chennai corridor to be modelled on the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor
Feasibility study of a Vizag-Chennai industrial corridor
Feasibility study of a SAIL steel plant in Kurnool district
x: The SAIL steel plant feasibility study is for YSR district, not Kurnool; the Duggirajupatnam port and the DMIC-modelled Vizag-Chennai corridor study are correct.

s: Where was a major port to be developed under Schedule XIII of the AP Reorganisation Act?
x: Schedule XIII commits a major port at Duggirajupatnam.

s: On which corridor is the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor in Schedule XIII modelled?
x: The corridor is modelled on the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC).

s: For which district was the SAIL steel plant feasibility study for Andhra Pradesh under the Thirteenth Schedule?
x: AP's steel plant study is for YSR district (Kadapa); Khammam is Telangana's plant.

s:
Consider the following statements about the South Coast Railway zone:
1. Its headquarters is at Visakhapatnam.
2. It is India's 18th railway zone.
3. It became operational on 1 June 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: South Coast Railway, India's 18th zone, is headquartered at Visakhapatnam and is operational from 1 June 2026, not 2024.

s: With which place is the refinery and petrochemical complex under the Thirteenth Schedule linked?
x: The refinery and petrochemical complex is at Kakinada, a GAIL-HPCL 50:50 JV.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Thirteenth Schedule infrastructure commitments to Andhra Pradesh?
o: International-standard airports at Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati
Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor modelled on DMIC
x: Metro rail is for Visakhapatnam and the Vijayawada-Guntur-Tenali region, not Tirupati.

s: Which of the following was a Thirteenth Schedule commitment to Telangana and not to Andhra Pradesh?
o: Refinery and petrochemical complex at Kakinada
x: The NTPC 4,000 MW plant, a SAIL steel plant in Khammam and a Rail Coach Factory were Telangana items; the others were for AP.

s: Which of the following divisions is NOT part of the South Coast Railway zone?
x: South Coast Railway (HQ Visakhapatnam) has the Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam divisions; Secunderabad is not one of them.

s: Which companies formed a 50:50 joint venture for the petrochemical complex at Kakinada under the Thirteenth Schedule commitments?
x: The Kakinada refinery and petrochemical complex is a GAIL-HPCL 50:50 joint venture.

s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule, the SAIL steel plant commitment to Telangana was for which district?
x: The SAIL steel plant for Telangana was in Khammam; Andhra Pradesh's study was for YSR district (Kadapa).

s: To which States was Special Category Status first given when it was introduced in 1969, in the Fifth Finance Commission era?
o: Jammu and Kashmir, Assam and Nagaland
Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Assam
x: Special Category Status began in 1969 for Jammu and Kashmir, Assam and Nagaland.

s: Which Finance Commission removed the distinction between special and general category States in tax devolution?
x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission (2015) removed the special/general distinction; AP then got special packages instead of SCS.

s: Which States, besides Andhra Pradesh, still demand Special Category Status (as of January 2026)?
x: AP, Bihar and Odisha still demand SCS.

s: Under which provision is Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh provided?
o: the Thirteenth Schedule of the APRA 2014
None of these; it is not in the Act
x: The APRA 2014 has no SCS clause; the demand rests on assurances outside the Act.

s: What is the CSS funding pattern (Centre:State) for Special Category States and for other States respectively?
x: Special Category States get a 90:10 pattern, against 60:40 under the ordinary CSS pattern.

s:
Consider the following statements about externally aided projects (EAPs) under the special assistance measure for Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Centre repays the loans and interest of EAPs signed between 2015-16 and 2019-20.
2. The Centre bears 60 per cent of the EAP cost.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct; statement 2 is wrong because the Centre bears 90 per cent of the EAP cost.

s: On which date did the Union Cabinet approve the special assistance measure in lieu of SCS?
x: The Union Cabinet approved it on 15 March 2017.

s: Under the special assistance measure of 2017, what share of the remaining cost of the irrigation component of Polavaram does the Centre fund?
x: Component 2 of the package: the Centre funds 100% of the remaining cost of Polavaram's irrigation component from 1 April 2014.

s: Which was the largest item of central transfers to Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24 (RE)?
x: In 2023-24 RE the order was FC grants, then other grants-in-aid, then EAP funds, then small savings.

s: Polavaram was declared a national project under which provision of the A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Section 90 declares Polavaram a national project (APPSC 2021, 2022). Some sources wrongly print Section 89, which extends the KWDT term. Section 46 concerns finance/backward areas and Section 94 fiscal incentives and capital support.

s: The irrigation potential of the Polavaram Project extends over which set of erstwhile districts?
o: East Godavari, Visakhapatnam, West Godavari and Krishna
x: The stated irrigation coverage is 2.91 lakh hectares in erstwhile East Godavari, Visakhapatnam, West Godavari and Krishna districts.

s: Which institution cleared the structural safety of the new spillway blocks of the Polavaram Project in April 2026?
x: The Central Water Commission cleared the structural safety of the new spillway blocks, in line with the Dam Safety Act, 2021.

s:
Consider the following statements about the implementation of the Polavaram Project:
1. Land acquisition and delays in rehabilitation and resettlement funding have caused friction.
2. Shortage of coal for thermal power generation has caused friction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The friction points are revised cost estimates, land acquisition and R&R funding delays; coal shortage is not one of them. So only statement 1 is correct.

s: Who executes the irrigation component of the Polavaram national project?
o: Government of Andhra Pradesh, on behalf of GoI, seeking reimbursement
Government of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh jointly
x: The Government of AP executes the irrigation component on behalf of the Government of India and seeks reimbursement or advances. CWC clears safety and designs; the Ministry does not execute directly; Telangana has no executing role.

s: What is the irrigation potential of the Polavaram Project?
x: Polavaram will irrigate about 2.91 lakh ha in former East Godavari, Visakhapatnam, West Godavari and Krishna districts.

s: How much did the Union Budget 2026-27 provide for Polavaram towards its revised cost?
x: The Budget of 2 February 2026 gave ₹3,320 crore for Polavaram's revised cost.

s: Up to what storage level did the Union Budget 2026-27 provide for the Polavaram project?
x: The Budget of 2 February 2026 gave Rs 3,320 crore towards the revised cost for storage up to +41.15 m.

s: Who are the members of the Apex Council under Section 84 of the AP Reorganisation Act?
o: The Prime Minister and both Chief Ministers
The Union Water Resources Minister alone
The Union Water Resources Minister and both Chief Ministers
Both Chief Ministers and both Governors
x: The Apex Council has 3 members: the Union Water Resources Minister (chair) and both Chief Ministers.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Godavari River Management Board (GRMB)?
x: GRMB is headquartered in Telangana and KRMB in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Within what period were the river management boards under Section 85 to be set up?
x: The boards were to be set up within 60 days, with security by CISF.

s: Under Schedule XI principles, without whose sanction can no new project on the Krishna or Godavari be taken up?
x: No new project on Krishna or Godavari can come up without Apex Council sanction.

s: Which Ministry notified the jurisdiction of the Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards in July 2021?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: The Ministry of Jal Shakti issued two gazette notifications on 15 July 2021 setting the jurisdiction of GRMB and KRMB.

s: In which year were the jurisdictions of the GRMB and KRMB notified by the Centre through gazette notifications?
x: Though the boards were set up in 2014, their jurisdiction was notified only on 15 July 2021.

s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026, which place was named as Andhra Pradesh's sole and permanent capital?
x: The 2026 amendment amended Section 5 to name Amaravati as the sole and permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh.

s: From which date does the A.P. Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026, making Amaravati the sole and permanent capital, take effect retrospectively?
x: It is retrospective from 2 June 2024, the day the 10-year common-capital period ended. 1 March 2014 is the assent date, 2 June 2014 the appointed day, and 3 March 2022 the High Court order.

s: Andhra Pradesh complained that after bifurcation it got about 46% of revenue but inherited about what share of the debt?
x: Assets followed location but debts followed population, so AP got about 46% of revenue but inherited 58% of the debt.

s: Which date was the appointed day under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: The Act received assent on 1 March 2014 and the appointed day was 2 June 2014.

s: The financial division provisions of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 lie in which Sections?
x: Sections 47-64 deal with the apportionment of assets and liabilities; Sections 76-83 are about services.

s: On what basis are land, stores and goods situated within a particular State divided?
x: Under Section 48, land, stores and goods located inside a State are assigned on the basis of location.

s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, on what basis are arrears of taxes other than property taxes divided?
x: Section 50 divides arrears of other taxes by place of assessment; refunds of such taxes follow the population ratio.

s: Which of the following is the rule for dividing commercial undertakings under the AP Reorganisation Act?
o: Operational units follow the population ratio, while headquarters follow location.
Operational units follow location, while headquarters follow the population ratio.
Both operational units and headquarters are divided only by population ratio.
Both operational units and headquarters follow the place of assessment.
x: Under Section 53, operational units of commercial undertakings follow location, whereas headquarters are divided according to the population ratio.

s: Which fund was divided between AP and Telangana on the basis of area ratio, not population?
x: The Calamity Relief Fund is the only fund split by area ratio; most other items went by population or location.

s: Under Section 58, on what basis are Provident Fund balances divided?
o: The State to which the employee is allotted
x: Provident Fund follows the State the employee is allotted to, not the population ratio.

s: How were cash balances held in treasuries divided at bifurcation?
o: In the population ratio, by adjustment in RBI books
By the location of the treasury
By the place of assessment of taxes
x: Treasury cash balances were apportioned in the population ratio and adjusted in RBI books, with no physical transfer.

s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Seventh Schedule relates to which of the following?
o: List of institutions whose headquarters are divided by population ratio
List of coal linkages between the two States
List of funds in the Public Account
x: The Seventh Schedule is the List of Funds in the Public Account, including provident, pension and insurance funds.

s: Under Section 58, which of the following does provident fund liability follow?
o: The two States in the population ratio
The State where the employee was born
The State where the employee last served
The State to which the employee is permanently allotted
x: Provident fund liability follows the State to which the employee is permanently allotted.

s: Which of the following institution–Schedule pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh — Ninth Schedule
Shilparamam Arts, Crafts and Cultural Society — Ninth Schedule
x: The Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh is an example of a Ninth Schedule institution. APSFC is also in the Ninth Schedule, while APSCHE and Shilparamam are examples under the Tenth Schedule.

s: Andhra Pradesh invokes which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act to bring unscheduled institutions into Schedule IX or X?
x: AP invokes Section 66 to bring institutions not in any Schedule into Schedule IX or X.

s: Under which Schedule is APSFC listed, and which Section governs its division?
x: APSFC is a Schedule IX body, and its division falls under Section 70.

s: How many Schedule X institutions did the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 list as enacted?
x: The Act as passed listed 107 Schedule X institutions; 35 more added in May 2015 made it 142. Schedule IX has 91.

s: How many government companies and corporations are listed in Schedule IX of the AP Reorganisation Act?
x:
Most books and reports: 91 Schedule IX bodies. Strictly, the Ninth Schedule of the Act as enacted lists 89 (AP Reorganisation Act 2014, Ninth Schedule).
Schedule IX is usually cited as listing 91 government companies and corporations; the Act as enacted lists 89 (entries 1-89), the rest were added later.

s: Which Section governs the continuance of facilities of Schedule X institutions for both States?
x: Section 75 governs Schedule X institutions; Sections 68 and 53 relate to Schedule IX bodies.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Schedule X of the AP Reorganisation Act?
o: It lists State institutions whose facilities continue for both States
Shilparamam Arts, Crafts and Cultural Society is listed in it
x: APSFC is a Schedule IX body; APSCHE and Shilparamam are Schedule X institutions.

s: How many institutions did Schedule X of the AP Reorganisation Act have after 35 more were added by notification in May 2015?
x: Schedule X had 107 institutions as enacted; 35 more were added on 7 May 2015, making 142.

s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides that the Ninth Schedule companies and corporations continue to function?
x: Section 68 lets Schedule IX bodies continue to function; Section 53 governs their division.

s: Within what period were the terms for continuing facilities of Schedule X institutions to be fixed?
x: For Schedule X institutions, the terms for continuing facilities to the other State were to be fixed within one year.

s: Why is Andhra Pradesh Bhavan, New Delhi divided by population ratio under the Act?
o: It is a Schedule IX corporation.
It lies outside the undivided State of Andhra Pradesh.
It was established by the Centre after bifurcation.
x: Since Andhra Pradesh Bhavan lies outside the undivided State, the Act applies the population-ratio principle. Telangana nevertheless claims it as Nizam's property.

s: In the case of APSCHE, the Supreme Court applied which combination of principles?
o: Location rule for assets and population ratio for cash and bank balances
Population ratio for assets and location rule for cash and bank balances
Domicile rule for assets and area ratio for balances
Equal division for both assets and cash balances
x: For APSCHE, the Supreme Court applied the location rule to assets and divided cash and bank balances according to the population ratio.

s: What did the Union Home Ministry do after the APSCHE ruling?
o: Applied the same formula to other Schedule X institutions
Referred all institutions to a High Court judge
Divided all institutions by area ratio
x: The Union Home Ministry applied the same APSCHE formula to other Schedule X institutions.

s: Under Section 70, to whom is the APSFC division scheme referred if it is not approved by shareholders?
x: An approved scheme goes to the Centre for sanction; if not approved, it goes to a High Court judge, whose settlement is final.

s: When did the Andhra Pradesh government move the Supreme Court seeking quick division of Schedule IX and Schedule X assets?
x: In December 2022 AP moved the Supreme Court for expeditious division of Schedule IX and X assets.

s: In which year did the Supreme Court rule that APSCHE assets go by location while its cash and bank balances are shared by population ratio?
x: The Supreme Court's APSCHE ruling of 2016 set the location rule for assets and population ratio for cash balances.

s: In what ratio (AP : Telangana) did the Union Home Ministry order on APSCHE share the cash balances?
x: The MHA order gave APSCHE assets to the State of location and shared cash balances 52:48 between AP and Telangana.

s: On what ground does Telangana claim the AP Bhavan in New Delhi?
o: It was built by the undivided State after 1956
It is a Schedule IX corporation
It was the property of the Nizam
It lies within the Telangana quota under Article 371D
x: AP Bhavan lies outside the undivided State and so goes by population ratio, but Telangana claims it as the Nizam's property.

s: Which of the following were allocated on the recommendations of the Pratyush Sinha Committee?
o: Assets and liabilities of Schedule IX companies
x: Pratyush Sinha handled All India Services officers; Kamalanathan handled State-level employees and Sheela Bhide handled Schedule IX companies and corporations.

s: Who chaired the committee associated with the partition of the 1953 Andhra State?
x: The 1953 Andhra State partition committee was chaired by T. T. Krishnamachari.

s: Which of the following were allocated on the recommendations of the Kamalanathan Committee?
x: C.R. Kamalanathan headed the committee on State-level employees; Pratyush Sinha handled All India Services.

s: The Sheela Bhide Committee recommended the division of how many of the 91 Schedule IX bodies?
x: It recommended division of 89 of the 91 Schedule IX bodies; Telangana opposed its recommendations on 22.

s:
Consider the following pairs of committees and their subjects:
1. Sheela Bhide Committee – Schedule IX companies and corporations
2. Pratyush Sinha Committee – All India Services officers
3. Kamalanathan Committee – Schedule X institutions
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
x: Sheela Bhide dealt with Schedule IX bodies and Pratyush Sinha with AIS officers; Kamalanathan dealt with State-level employees, not Schedule X.

s: Under which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 was the Pratyush Sinha Committee on All India Services officers formed?
x: The Pratyush Sinha Committee on allocation of IAS, IPS and IFoS officers was formed under Section 80.

s: Disputes concerning seniority and pensions are associated with which provision and institution?
o: Section 59 and the Eighth Schedule; AP Reorganisation Tribunal
Section 66 and the Ninth Schedule; Central Administrative Tribunal
Section 95 and the Eleventh Schedule; Finance Commission
Section 76 and the Tenth Schedule; Election Commission
x: Disputes over seniority and pensions under Section 59 and the Eighth Schedule have contributed to the backlog of the AP Reorganisation Tribunal.

s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 creates separate State cadres of the IAS, IPS and IFoS?
x: Section 76 creates separate AIS cadres under the 1954/1966 Cadre Rules; Section 77 deals with State employees.

s: An employee who did not exercise an option for a State was allotted by the Centre primarily on the basis of:
x: Employees had to opt for a State; those who did not were allotted by the Centre on the basis of native or domicile status.

s: In which Part of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 are the Provisions as to Services contained?
x: Part VIII (Sections 76-83) is Provisions as to Services; Part XI covers higher education.

s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act deals with State employees and does not apply to All India Services?
x: Section 77 covers State employees and does not apply to All India Services; Section 76 creates the AIS State cadres.

s: Who headed the one-member committee on AIS allotment cases set up by DoPT in March 2024?
x: After the Telangana High Court's 3 January 2024 order, DoPT set up the one-member Deepak Khandekar committee in March 2024.

s: The Centre could set up Advisory Committees on employee allocation within how many days of enactment?
x: Advisory Committees could be set up within 30 days of enactment.

s: For how long did staff of PSUs and corporations stay in place after bifurcation, under Section 82?
x: Under Section 82 staff of PSUs and corporations stayed where they were for one year, and the corporation itself decided the division.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about power sharing under the Twelfth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act?
o: Central Generating Station power is shared on the DISCOMs' actual consumption over the last five years
Power from APGENCO plants is allocated by population ratio
Andhra Pradesh got about 46 per cent of the power
Andhra Pradesh had about 58 per cent of the population
x: APGENCO plants are divided by location (with existing PPAs continuing), not by population ratio; the other statements are correct.

s: For how many years does a deficit State have a first right of refusal over the surplus power of the other State?
x: The deficit State enjoys the first right of refusal over the other State's surplus power for 10 years.

s: What is Telangana's equity share in Singareni Collieries Company Limited under the Twelfth Schedule?
x: Telangana holds 51 per cent and the Government of India 49 per cent of SCCL; Andhra Pradesh holds none.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the unresolved bifurcation issues?
o: APGENCO says Telangana's DISCOMs owe it for power supplied after bifurcation
Andhra Pradesh holds 49% equity in SCCL
APSFC division is pending under Section 70
x: SCCL equity is 51% Telangana and 49% Government of India, so AP holds no equity.

s: Under Section 95, for how long did the Article 371D admission quotas and common admission process in higher, technical and medical institutions continue?
x: Section 95 continued the 371D quotas and common admission process for ten years in government and private, aided and unaided institutions.

s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act amended Article 371D to cover "Andhra Pradesh or Telangana"?
x: Section 97 amended Article 371D; Section 95 continued the admission quotas.

s: In which Part of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 is Section 95, on equal opportunities for quality higher education, placed?
x: Section 95 is in Part XI (Access to Higher Education); Part VIII deals with services.

s: Which of the following pairs about the undivided AP-Telangana institutions is correctly matched?
o: Basis demanded by Telangana – population ratio
Number of undivided corporations and institutions – more than 140
Basis demanded by Andhra Pradesh – location
x: More than 140 corporations and institutions worth over Rs 39,000 crore remain undivided. Telangana insists on location, while AP seeks the 58:42 population ratio.

s: Which of the following is directly affected by the more than Rs 24,000 crore of unapportioned public debt on Andhra Pradesh's books?
o: Authority to divide Schedule X employees
Right of refusal over surplus power
x: The unapportioned debt eats into Andhra Pradesh's borrowing room under the FRBM framework.

s: Which body directed Andhra Pradesh to pay Telangana its share of the central subsidy credited to AP?
x: The Southern Zonal Council directed AP to pay Telangana its share, which remains unpaid.

s: What amount was released to Andhra Pradesh between 2 June 2014 and 2016-17 towards the revenue deficit gap?
x: The amount released was Rs 3,979.50 crore. The figure of Rs 4,117.89 crore was the Centre's calculated gap, while Rs 16,078 crore was Andhra Pradesh's claim.

s: What did Andhra Pradesh claim as its true 2014-15 resource gap?
x: AP claimed about Rs 16,078 crore, whereas the Centre's standardised calculation gave about Rs 4,117.89 crore.

s: The amount of Rs 3,979 crore was counted as the revenue deficit grant within which measure announced for Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Rs 3,979 crore was counted within the Special Assistance Measure, or SAM, for which Rs 24,350 crore was announced.

s: What was the Centre's calculation of Andhra Pradesh's 2014-15 resource gap?
x: The Centre calculated Rs 4,117.89 crore using standardised accounting; AP claimed Rs 16,078 crore and Rs 3,979.50 crore was released.

s: What was the size of the Special Assistance Measure for Andhra Pradesh?
x: SAM was Rs 24,350 crore, within which the Rs 3,979 crore revenue deficit grant was counted.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Special Category Status and the Special Assistance Measure?
o: Special Category Status was promised on the floor of Parliament for five years
Andhra Pradesh has argued that the Special Assistance Measure has statutory permanence
The Centre cited the Fourteenth Finance Commission while denying Special Category Status
Under the Special Assistance Measure, the Centre funds the 90 per cent grant equivalent only for Externally Aided Projects
x: AP says the Special Assistance Measure lacks statutory permanence, so the statement that AP argued it has statutory permanence is wrong. SCS was promised in Parliament for five years and denied citing the 14th FC, and SAM gives a 90% grant equivalent only for EAPs.

s: To what level did the Fourteenth Finance Commission raise the States' share in the divisible pool from 32 per cent?
x: The Fourteenth FC (2015-20) raised the States' share from 32 to 42 per cent and removed the general/special category distinction.

s: How much did Andhra Pradesh say it lost after the Sixteenth Finance Commission discontinued revenue deficit grants for all States?
x: AP said it lost up to Rs 38,000 crore. Rs 22,113 crore was the 14th FC RD grant; Rs 3,979 crore was the 2014-15 resource-gap release; Rs 48,000 crore is the projected 2025-26 revenue deficit.

s: According to the Andhra Pradesh Finance Minister's assessment, the revenue deficit was about Rs 16,000 crore during 2014-19 and was projected to widen to what amount in 2025-26?
x: The revenue deficit was stated to be about Rs 16,000 crore during 2014-19 and projected to reach about Rs 48,000 crore in 2025-26.

s: After the 16th Finance Commission ended revenue deficit grants, the Centre sanctioned how much for Amaravati to help AP tide over?
x: The Centre sanctioned Rs 15,000 crore for Amaravati plus other assistance; Rs 38,000 crore is AP's claimed loss and Rs 22,113 crore the 14th FC RD grant.

s: How are Special Assistance for Capital Investment (SASCI) 50-year interest-free loans to Andhra Pradesh treated?
o: part of the revenue deficit grant
outside the 3% of GSDP fiscal-deficit cap
off-budget borrowings reported by the CAG for March 2023
part of the 3% of GSDP fiscal-deficit cap
x: SASCI 50-year interest-free loans are treated as outside the 3% of GSDP fiscal-deficit cap.

s: Which Finance Commission removed the distinction between general and special category States?
x: The 14th Finance Commission (2015-20) removed the general/special category distinction.

s: For which projects did the Centre provide a 90% grant equivalent under the Special Assistance Measure?
x: SAM gave a 90% grant equivalent only for Externally Aided Projects (EAPs).

s: Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh was promised in Parliament for how many years?
x: SCS was promised for 5 years but denied, citing the 14th Finance Commission.

s: Which Finance Commission recommended a post-devolution revenue deficit grant of Rs 22,113 crore for Andhra Pradesh?
x: The 14th Finance Commission (2015-20) gave AP a post-devolution revenue deficit grant of Rs 22,113 crore.

s: Which Finance Commission discontinued revenue deficit grants for all States?
x: The 16th Finance Commission was the first to end revenue deficit grants for all States; AP says it lost up to Rs 38,000 crore.

s: How much interest did Andhra Pradesh pay in 2024-25?
x: AP paid Rs 32,944 crore as interest in 2024-25, a committed cost that crowds out capital outlay.

s: Disputes over financial assets and liabilities arising from bifurcation are to be settled through a Central order on whose advice under Section 47(4)?
o: Advice of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Advice of the Reserve Bank of India
Advice of the Finance Commission alone
x: Section 47(4) provides for a Central order on the advice of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in disputes over financial assets and liabilities.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2014-15 resource gap?
o: AP claimed a gap of Rs 16,078 crore
The Centre's figure excluded new commitments
The CAG issues the final order on disputes under Section 47(4)
x: Under Section 47(4) the Centre issues the order on the advice of the CAG; the CAG only advises.

s: According to the Fourteenth Finance Commission's estimate, how much did the tax-arrears and refund anomaly cost Andhra Pradesh?
x: The anomaly was estimated to have cost Andhra Pradesh about Rs 3,900 crore.

s: On what basis are public debt and Public Account liabilities of the successor States generally apportioned under Section 54 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: the geographical area of the successor States
the location of the project financed by the liability
x: Section 54 provides for the division of public debt and Public Account liabilities according to the population ratio, subject to the specific treatment of loans re-lent for activities confined to one State.

s: Under Section 55 of the AP Reorganisation Act, on what basis are floating loans not raised for one particular State divided?
x: Section 55 keeps a floating loan with the State for whose purposes it was raised and divides the rest by population ratio.

s: Which of the following pairs about the division between AP and Telangana is correctly matched?
o: Basis for dividing revenue assets – population
x: Debt was divided by population, so AP took 58% of it, while revenue assets were allocated by location and AP got only 46%.

s: Under Section 54, what happens to loans re-lent for an activity located in one State?
x: Public debt goes by population ratio, but loans re-lent for an activity in one State stay with that State.

s:
Consider the following statements about the division of tax arrears and refunds after bifurcation:
1. Arrears of property tax or land revenue are divided according to the State where the property lies.
2. Refunds of other taxes collected in excess are divided by population ratio.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are true: property-tax arrears follow the property's location, while refunds of other taxes follow the population ratio.

s: What anomaly arose from the different rules governing tax arrears and tax refunds after bifurcation?
o: Arrears followed the location of property, while all refunds followed the location of industrial units.
Arrears and refunds were both assigned to the Union Government.
Arrears generally followed the place of assessment, while refunds followed the population ratio.
Both arrears and refunds followed the population ratio, causing no dispute.
x: Arrears of other taxes generally followed the place of assessment, which was mostly Hyderabad, whereas refunds of other taxes followed the population ratio. This difference was considered disadvantageous to Andhra Pradesh.

s: After bifurcation, on what basis were arrears of taxes other than property taxes divided between AP and Telangana?
x: Arrears of other taxes follow the place of assessment (mostly Hyderabad), while their refunds follow population.

s: Under Section 53(1) of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, to whom does the right to recover deferred taxes of industrial units go?
o: The State where the unit is located
x: The right to recover deferred taxes of an industrial unit belongs to the State where the unit is located; note that the Act puts this under Section 51(1) (loans and advances), not Section 53(1).

s: Pensions already sanctioned before the appointed day are divided between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana on which basis?
x: Under Section 59 and the Eighth Schedule, pensions sanctioned before the appointed day are shared according to the population ratio of 58.32:41.68.

s: On what basis were APGENCO power plants divided under the Twelfth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: APGENCO plants go by location and existing PPAs with the DISCOMs continue.

s: How much did the Union Power Ministry order Telangana to pay Andhra Pradesh on 29 August 2022?
x: The order was for Rs 6,756.92 crore (principal Rs 3,441.78 crore plus surcharge) within 30 days.

s:
Consider the following statements about the AP-Telangana power dues dispute:
1. Telangana counter-claimed Rs 12,940 crore.
2. The Telangana High Court set aside the Union Power Ministry's order in October 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Telangana counter-claimed Rs 12,940 crore and its High Court set aside the order on 19 October 2023; AP appealed to the Supreme Court.

s: Under the Twelfth Schedule, what happened to existing power purchase agreements with DISCOMs?
o: They were renegotiated by population ratio
They were transferred to the Centre
x: APGENCO plants were divided by location and existing PPAs with DISCOMs continue.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the choice of Andhra Pradesh's capital?
o: The Capital City Advisory Committee was chaired by P. Narayana
P. Narayana was the Municipal Administration Minister
The Capital City Advisory Committee backed the Vijayawada-Guntur region
The final decision to locate the capital at Amaravati was taken by the Central Government
x: The AP Cabinet, not the Centre, chose Amaravati; the committee chaired by Municipal Administration Minister P. Narayana backed the Vijayawada-Guntur region.

s: On which study was the three-capitals proposal of 2020 principally based?
o: Capital City Advisory Committee and World Bank study
Sivaramakrishnan Committee and APCRDA master plan
G.N. Rao Committee and BCG study
x: The three-capitals proposal was based on the G.N. Rao Committee and the BCG study.

s: Within what period did the Expert Committee under Section 6 of the AP Reorganisation Act have to submit its report?
x: The committee, constituted by the Centre, had to report within six months; it opposed a single super capital.

s: Which committee was constituted under Section 6 to identify suitable locations for the capital of Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation?
x: The Expert Committee under Section 6 was chaired by K.C. Sivaramakrishnan and was asked to identify locations for the new capital.

s: Who headed the Capital City Advisory Committee set up by the AP government?
x: Municipal Administration Minister P. Narayana headed the State committee, which backed the Vijayawada-Guntur region.

s: On the banks of which river is Amaravati, the capital of Andhra Pradesh, located?
x: The AP Cabinet chose Amaravati on the Krishna, between Vijayawada and Guntur.

s: What did the K.C. Sivaramakrishnan Committee oppose in its report on the new capital of Andhra Pradesh?
o: A capital in the Rayalaseema region
A single 'super capital', because of ecological fears
Any land pooling for the capital
Locating the High Court outside the capital
x: The Section 6 expert committee reported in August 2014 and opposed one large 'super capital' due to ecological fears.

s: What does Section 94(4) of the AP Reorganisation Act deal with?
o: Denotification of degraded forest land for the capital, if required
Constitution of the expert committee on the capital
x: Section 94(4) provides for denotifying degraded forest land for the capital; Section 5 is the common capital and Section 6 the expert committee.

s: Under which provision of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 is special financial support provided for essential facilities in the new capital?
x: Section 94(3) provides for special financial support for essential facilities in the new capital. Section 95 relates to higher-education quota provisions.

s: For how many years was Hyderabad to be the common capital under the AP Reorganisation Act?
x: Section 5 made Hyderabad the common capital for 10 years.

s: What was the Andhra Pradesh Government's estimate of the cost of building the new capital?
x: The State estimated about Rs 1.2 lakh crore, while the Centre's commitment was only about Rs 27,000 crore.

s: For what was the Rs 1,000 crore released later under Section 94(3) used?
o: Underground drainage works in Vijayawada and Guntur
x: Of the Rs 2,500 crore, Rs 1,500 crore was initial capital construction and Rs 1,000 crore went to UGD works in Vijayawada and Guntur.

s: What was the initial direct central grant for capital construction under Section 94(3)?
x: The initial grant was Rs 1,500 crore, followed by Rs 1,000 crore, totalling Rs 2,500 crore.

s: According to the Finance Ministry, after what was the balance Rs 1,000 crore to be released?
o: Utilisation certificates for the Rs 1,500 crore
NITI Aayog approval of the master plan
x: The Finance Ministry released the balance in phases only after utilisation certificates for the Rs 1,500 crore.

s: In 2018, Andhra Pradesh claimed which body had not rejected its utilisation certificates?
x: AP's position in 2018 was that NITI Aayog did not reject its UCs; the Centre said the UCs were incorrect.

s: How much is the World Bank and ADB assistance for Amaravati, on concessional terms of 0.6% plus TONA?
x: The World Bank and ADB assistance amounts to Rs 15,000 crore at 0.6% plus TONA; Rs 11,000 crore is the HUDCO loan.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: World Bank and ADB — Rs 7,387.70 crore infrastructure finance
HUDCO — Rs 11,000 crore term loan for urban infrastructure
NaBFID — Rs 11,000 crore concessional loan at 0.6% plus TONA
x: HUDCO sanctioned Rs 11,000 crore as a term loan for urban infrastructure. The other options interchange the lenders and amounts.

s: Between which two forms of capital assistance is the principal dispute between Andhra Pradesh and the Centre?
o: tax devolution or Finance Commission grants
non-repayable grants or loans supported by sovereign guarantees
foreign direct investment or equity shares
municipal bonds or State development loans
x: Andhra Pradesh sought non-repayable grants, whereas the Centre routed assistance through loans and sovereign guarantees, requiring approvals under Article 293(2).

s: Why has reliance on loans instead of grants for capital development been criticised?
o: It prevents all private investment in the capital
It transfers the entire capital expenditure to local governments
It increases repayment burdens and may crowd out welfare and development spending
It eliminates the need for utilisation certificates and audits
x: Borrowing instead of receiving grants adds repayment obligations and can reduce the fiscal space available for welfare and development expenditure.

s: In what form did the Union Budget 2024-25 promise Rs 15,000 crore for Amaravati?
x: The Budget promised Rs 15,000 crore of Centre-facilitated multilateral support.

s: Under which Article is central approval required for State loans backed by sovereign guarantees for the capital?
x: Loans with sovereign guarantees need approval under Article 293(2).

o: Amaravati was to be the legislative capital
Visakhapatnam was to be the judicial capital
Kurnool was to be the judicial capital
Visakhapatnam was to be the executive capital

o: AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020
x: The APRA (Amendment) Act, 2026 made Amaravati the sole capital, alongside ₹15,000 crore of fast-tracked central assistance.

s: Where was the foundation stone of Amaravati laid on 22 October 2015?
x: PM Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone at Uddandarayunipalem on the Krishna in Guntur district.

s: On which date did the APCRDA Act, 2014 come into force?

x: Consent for about 33,000 acres had been obtained by March 2015.

x: On 3 March 2022 the AP High Court struck down the CRDA Repeal Act (2020).

o: Exemption from capital gains tax and stamp duty on first sale
Income tax holiday for ten years
Exemption from GST on farm inputs

x: The capital was planned within the original 29 villages; in March 2026 the CPI(M) asked for a single-phase capital there.

x: HUDCO is a domestic lender, so its loans are not external assistance; AIIB, UNDP and JICA are external lenders.

x: APILIP-II is a JICA-funded irrigation project; the World Bank funds APIIATP, not APILIP-II.

s: Which of the following does AIIB assistance in Andhra Pradesh support?
x: AIIB supports urban water supply and sewerage projects; JICA funds APILIP-II, NDB the roads and ADB the VCIC.

x: VCIC is ADB-funded. JICA funds APILIP-II, KfW the Green Energy Corridor Phase-I, and NDB the road projects.

s: Which of the following projects in Andhra Pradesh is funded by the World Bank?
o: AP Irrigation and Livelihood Project Phase-II
x: AP Health Systems Strengthening is World Bank-funded; the Green Energy Corridor is KfW, APILIP-II is JICA and VCIC is ADB.

o: JICA — urban water supply and sewerage under AMRUT 2.0
NDB — AP Roads and Bridges Reconstruction and rural connectivity roads
KfW — AP Rural Inclusive Growth Project
x: NDB supports AP Roads and Bridges Reconstruction and Mandal Connectivity and Rural Connectivity Improvement projects. AIIB supports urban water and sewerage, JICA supports APILIP-II, and KfW supports the Green Energy Corridor.

s: Which agency funds the AP Climate Resilient Zero Budget Natural Farming (APCNF) project?
x: APCNF is funded by KfW (Germany), not the World Bank.

s: Which agency funded the South Asia Poverty Alleviation Programme (SAPAP) in Andhra Pradesh?
x: SAPAP was funded by the UNDP, the only UN agency among AP's external funders.

s: Which agency funds the Andhra Pradesh Rural Inclusive Growth Project implemented by SERP?
x: The AP Rural Inclusive Growth Project is a World Bank project implemented by SERP.

x: AP Health Systems Strengthening is a World Bank project.

s: After which cyclone was the AP Disaster Recovery Project taken up?
x: The AP Disaster Recovery Project was taken up after Cyclone Hudhud in 2014.

x: APIIATP focuses on climate resilience and productivity in 565 minor-tank villages across 22 districts.

o: World Bank AP Road Sector Project – 850 km

s: On which date did the AP Integrated Irrigation and Agriculture Transformation Project conclude?
x: APIIATP concluded on 31 October 2025 (SES 2025-26).

s: Which is the first of the five components of the AP Rural Inclusive Growth Project?
x: The project has five components, the first being value chain development; others include human development and implementation support.

s: How much World Bank financing was approved for the AP Rural Inclusive Growth Project of $107 million?
x: Approved on 19 December 2014, the project costs $107 million, of which the World Bank finances $75 million.

s: On which date did the Union Cabinet approve the Special Assistance Measure for AP, under which the Centre repays EAP loans?
x: The Special Assistance Measure was approved on 15 March 2017 in lieu of Special Category Status.

s:
Consider the following statements about EAP repayment under the Special Assistance Measure:
1. The Centre bears 90% of the EAP cost.
2. It covers EAPs signed between 2015-16 and 2019-20.
3. The largest disbursement was for the Health Systems Strengthening project.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Centre bears 90% of the cost of EAPs signed in 2015-16 to 2019-20; the largest disbursement was for VCIC (₹1,859 crore), not Health Systems Strengthening (₹935 crore).

s: Under the Special Assistance Measure, the Centre reported disbursing loans for how many EAPs in AP?
x: The Centre reported disbursing ₹7,798 crore of loans for 17 EAPs in AP.

s: Among the 17 EAPs for which the Centre disbursed loans in Andhra Pradesh, which received the largest amount?
o: AP Integrated Irrigation and Agriculture Transformation Project
